To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a single global objective function for joint model-policy optimization that can be used to train a model-based RL agent.

(1) model-based reinforcement learning is often done in an inconsistent manner, where models are trained to minimize prediction error, while policies are trained to maximize reward; (2) we propose a joint model-policy optimization algorithm, MnM, that trains the model to maximize the performance of the policy; and (3) MnM is conceptually similar in spirit to GANs, and is a global lower-bound on expected return under certain assumptions.

we introduce a novel joint model-policy optimization algorithm for model-based reinforcement learning that mends the objective mis-match of prior work, and that our algorithm achieves state of the art performance on a suite of continuous control benchmarks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) How can we design an objective that jointly trains a model and a policy, so that both components improve the expected return?
the following questions: (i) How do we train a model to produce transitions that yield good policies? (ii) How do we use the model to improve the policy?
the objective mismatch in model-based RL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a joint optimization framework that mends the objective gap between the model and the RL policy, and we show how to use the resulting algorithm for model-based reinforcement learning.
we propose an algorithm to jointly optimize the policy and the model, and this algorithm has a global lower bound of expected return.
we propose a joint optimization objective to improve the performance of a model based RL algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MnM is a model-based algorithm with a policy that learns from its own experience and the model.
we propose a single global objective for model-based RL that can be used to jointly optimize a model and a policy, such that the model is useful to the policy.
MnM is an RL agent that uses a model for planning, but the agent is also learning to detect the errors of the model and to avoid them.
The main takeaway from our work is that

model-based RL can be formulated as a global optimization problem that jointly trains the model and policy, and that the objective can be made tight by using a classifier to detect when the model fails.
the objective mismatch between model and policy training can be fixed with a single, tight lower bound on the expected return of the resulting policy.

it is possible to jointly optimize a model and a policy in a way that improves the model and improves policy performance, without requiring any additional data beyond that required for model training alone.
